 60 days left: KRA issues warning as tax amnesty deadline nears
 Sunday 01st November, 2026 11:21 AM | 
 By Emmanuel Rono 
 A well-designed poster by KRA to illustrate Tax amnesty exercise. PHOTO/@KRACare/X 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has warned Kenyans against waiting until the last minute to file their outstanding taxes as its Tax Amnesty Programme, which offers a 100 per cent waiver on eligible penalties, interest and fines, nears its end.
 In a notice issued on Saturday, November 1, 2026, KRA urged individuals and businesses with outstanding tax obligations to take advantage of the programme before the December 31, 2026 deadline.
 The authority said taxpayers seeking to benefit from the amnesty must file all outstanding tax returns and settle their principal tax by the end of the year. 
 “With just 60 days left, time is running out to benefit from a 100% waiver on eligible penalties, interest and fines,” KRA stated.
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) statement on Sunday, November 1, 2026. PHOTO/Screengrab by People Daily Digital/@KRACare/X 
 The taxman cautioned taxpayers against waiting until the last minute, urging them to regularise their tax affairs before the programme expires.
 The initiative is intended to give eligible taxpayers an opportunity to clear outstanding tax obligations while benefiting from relief on accumulated penalties, interest and fines.
 KRA reiterated that the waiver applies to eligible penalties, interest and fines, meaning taxpayers must meet the programme’s conditions to qualify.
 Taxpayers can access further information about eligibility requirements and the application process through the authority’s official website.
 The deadline for the Tax Amnesty Programme is December 31, 2026.
 Who qualifies for the amnesty? 
 The programme was reintroduced through the Finance Act, 2026, which amended Section 37E of the Tax Procedures Act. 
 Taxpayers whose principal tax for periods ending December 31, 2025, was fully paid by that date do not need to apply for the waiver. 
 KRA office building. PHOTO/@KRACorporate/X 
 KRA says the related penalties and interest are processed automatically through iTax. 
 Those who only have outstanding late-filing penalties can also qualify by filing all pending returns for the qualifying periods, including nil returns. 
 However, tax liabilities arising from January 1, 2026, onwards do not qualify for the amnesty. Customs duties administered under the East African Community Customs Management Act are also excluded. 
 How taxpayers can clear outstanding tax 
 Taxpayers who still owe principal tax have two options for settling their debts. 
 They can make a lump-sum payment of the outstanding principal, after which the qualifying penalties, interest and fines are waived.
